articles.title: Meet your knowledge workspace
articles.summary: A shared home for the answers your people and agents need.

sections.heading: One workspace, many ways to find answers
sections.text: AgentZuno brings knowledge, source connections, and agent configurations into a familiar workspace. This public edition is both a product tour and a help center: the examples you explore are real explanations of how the product is being built.

sections.heading: Explore before you sign in
sections.text: Use the sidebar to browse knowledge, inspect example agents, explore planned connections, and search the help content. You do not need an account to take the tour.

sections.heading: Make it yours
sections.text: Sign in with a demo account to switch this same interface to that account’s own mock items. The guest collection is public product content; it is never another customer’s workspace.

articles.label: AgentZuno guide

articles.title: Explore first. Sign in when it is yours.
articles.summary: How public exploration and personal workspaces fit together.

sections.heading: Public by design
sections.text: The guest workspace contains only AgentZuno product guides and clearly labeled examples. It is available without registration. Opening a page, searching, and reading help do not require sign-in.

sections.heading: A clear change of context
sections.text: After sign-in, the workspace name, articles, agents, and tasks change to your account’s mock dataset. The Explore AgentZuno link opens the public help collection without replacing your own workspace.

sections.heading: A prototype, honestly labeled
sections.text: This build uses JSON fixtures and in-memory sessions. Demo accounts demonstrate the separation between users. They are not intended to hold real private or sensitive information. Production identity and persistent storage come later.

articles.label: AgentZuno guide

articles.title: Find your first answer
articles.summary: Use search, knowledge bases, and article links to explore.

sections.heading: Search across the workspace
sections.text: Open Search in the sidebar and type a phrase such as permissions, agents, or connections. Results match article titles, summaries, and content in your current workspace.

sections.heading: Browse by topic
sections.text: Knowledge bases group related articles. Choose a base to filter its articles, then open any title to read the full guide. Pages have their own URLs, so browser back and direct links work.

sections.heading: Keep the source close
sections.text: Every public guide is labeled as AgentZuno product content. Future imported sources should retain source attribution and permissions. This prototype does not connect to external services.

articles.label: AgentZuno guide

articles.title: Give useful knowledge a home
articles.summary: A simple structure for information your team can trust.

sections.heading: Start with an answer
sections.text: Organize articles around the question a reader is trying to answer. Use a specific title, a short summary, and clear sections. The examples in this workspace show that structure.

sections.heading: Group with intent
sections.text: Use a knowledge base for a stable topic, such as getting started, product guidance, or internal operations. Prefer a small number of useful categories to a long list of empty folders.

sections.heading: What works in this preview
sections.text: You can browse and search articles and filter by knowledge base. Editing, publication workflows, and version history are future features; the preview is read-only.

articles.label: AgentZuno guide

articles.title: Knowledge for any agent
articles.summary: Explore how agents can use a shared body of knowledge.

sections.heading: A shared source of truth
sections.text: The goal is to let people and agents work from the same curated knowledge. Agent configurations can describe a purpose, a knowledge scope, and rules about citing sources.

sections.heading: Inspect an example
sections.text: The Agents page contains example configurations you can open and read. They are product examples, not connected AI services. No model requests are executed in this preview.

sections.heading: Keep access aligned
sections.text: A future agent should receive only content available to its authenticated identity. Connecting an AI service will require an explicit implementation and a deliberate choice about where content is sent.

articles.label: AgentZuno guide

articles.title: Connect the tools your team uses
articles.summary: Connect ServiceNow knowledge, index it locally, and give agents controlled access.

sections.heading: Connect ServiceNow as a reader
sections.text: Ask your administrator to install the AgentZuno knowledge permission bridge, then connect with a delegated user OAuth token. Source-enforced reads evaluate ServiceNow ACLs and KB/article user criteria before returning content.

sections.heading: Import and index
sections.text: Preserve source knowledge-base names or bundle articles into an existing base. MongoDB stores snapshots and chunks; the worker uses local Ollama embeddings and Qdrant vector indexes. Connection status shows indexing progress.

sections.heading: Give agents access
sections.text: Create each agent and grant only the knowledge bases it needs. Tokens inherit the agent’s current permissions. Every source-enforced result is checked again in ServiceNow; cached vectors never grant access.

sections.heading: Other sources
sections.text: Use the Custom connection action for authorized JSON or HTTPS API snapshots. Custom imports use AgentZuno-managed permissions and do not synchronize source access rules.

articles.label: AgentZuno guide

articles.title: Try your own workspace with a demo account
articles.summary: Two accounts let you test a genuine change of context.

sections.heading: Choose a demo account
sections.text: Open Sign in and choose Alex or Jordan. The form shows the public demo credentials. Continue to enter that account’s workspace; you do not need to register or supply personal information.

sections.heading: Separate on the server
sections.text: A session cookie identifies the selected account. The API chooses that account’s JSON fixture on the server. Adding another user ID to a URL does not select their data.

sections.heading: Sign out to return to exploring
sections.text: Use Sign out in the account section. Your workspace returns to the public AgentZuno collection. Sessions are temporary and reset when the API container restarts.

articles.label: AgentZuno guide

articles.title: Answers about this preview
articles.summary: What is available, what is mocked, and what comes next.

sections.heading: Can I use this without an account?
sections.text: Yes. Public product articles, help, example agents, and the connection catalog are available to everyone. The app itself is the tour.

sections.heading: Can I add my own documents yet?
sections.text: Not yet. This version is read-only and uses mock JSON objects. Uploads, editing, and live source connections will be added as separate features.

sections.heading: Is this a live AI assistant?
sections.text: No. Agent cards describe example configurations. They do not run models or send your information to AI providers.

sections.heading: Why does my demo workspace look different?
sections.text: Each demo account has its own articles, agents, and tasks. The shared navigation stays the same, but the items shown are chosen from that account’s dataset.
